video.title: Elon's Anthropic Deal, The Next AI Monopoly?, "FDA for AI" Panic, Trading the AI Boom
video.display_title_html: Elon's Anthropic Deal, The Next AI Monopoly?, "FDA for AI" Panic, Trading the AI Boom

thesis: SpaceX leasing its Colossus data center to Anthropic reveals that AI revenue is gated by power and compute—not demand—and signals both Elon's emergence as a hyperscaler and Anthropic's trajectory toward an unprecedented, politically combustible monopoly.

chapters.title: Bestie intros! Thoughts on the LA mayor election
SpaceX-Anthropic deal, Elon Web Services, SpaceX IPO valuation, Anthropic's insane growth trajectory
Is Anthropic the next great monopoly? Early signals or major overreaction?
"FDA for AI" freakout, how the White House thinks about AI safety
Flipping AI's negative perception: Giving, healthcare and education innovation
Trading the AI market, state of the economy

insights.headline: AI revenue is gated by power, not demand
insights.body: Chamath argues Anthropic and OpenAI's revenue performance 'has nothing to do with demand, zero'—it is entirely constrained by data center supply and power. With infinite power, he says revenues would be even more parabolic, so beating or missing forecasts is meaningless.

insights.headline: Elon leases Colossus One to Anthropic
insights.body: Elon leased the entirety of his Colossus One data center to Anthropic, adding over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs and 300+ megawatts of capacity. The deal immediately let Anthropic double Claude Code rate limits, remove peak caps for paid users, and raise API volumes for Opus models.

insights.headline: Elon Web Services blunts the SpaceX bear case
insights.body: By leasing terrestrial compute, Elon creates a 'structural core business' that subsidizes training Grok and de-risks the speculative orbital-data-center valuation in the SpaceX roadshow. Brad estimates this adds $4-5B of incremental revenue this year on top of mid-$20B analyst estimates.

insights.headline: Anthropic ARR: $10B to $44B in four months
insights.body: Sachs says Anthropic grew from roughly $10B ARR on Jan 1 to $30B by March 31, then accelerated to $44B in April—after three years of 10x annual growth. He calls it growth at scale nobody in Silicon Valley has ever seen.

insights.headline: Anthropic could become the biggest monopoly ever
insights.body: Sachs argues if Anthropic sustains its exponential to ~$100B ARR this year and a trillion by 2027, it would be the most valuable tech company in history—possibly worth more than the rest of the Mag7 combined. Chamath notes the Mag7 total only ~$2.3-2.35T, so it would be the 'Mag 1.'

insights.headline: The 'Safe Oil' Rockefeller thought experiment
insights.body: Sachs argues if John D. Rockefeller had been good at PR, he would have rebranded Standard Oil as 'Safe Oil,' demanded a government agency to regulate kerosene safety, and called himself an effective altruist—distracting everyone from the monopoly he was building. His point: safety rhetoric can mask consolidation.

insights.headline: 'FDA for AI' was largely fabricated news
insights.body: Both Sachs and Brad spoke to Kevin Hassett, who said he only invoked the FDA analogy to mean labs should show models for coordination—not an approval regime. Sachs traces the panic to a New York Times piece and Andrew Ross Sorkin commentary that 'took on a life of its own'; Susie Wiles' statement shot it down.

insights.headline: KYC, not pre-approval, for frontier models
insights.body: Chamath and Sachs converge on requiring know-your-customer wrappers before granting API access to powerful models like Mythos—especially during preview periods—so labs can screen out state actors. Brad notes labs already track API use and flag suspicious activity to government.

insights.headline: Cyber capabilities in every frontier model within months
insights.body: Sachs says within three to six months all major frontier labs, plus Chinese and open-source models, will have Mythos-level cyber capabilities. Because offense and defense use the same toolset, he calls for getting these tools into cybersecurity firms like CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks first.

insights.headline: Data center protests are organized, not local
insights.body: Brad argues the protests delaying nearly half of the ~9 gigawatts coming online this year aren't organic—they're highly organized activists moving across the country, the same playbook that killed US fission reactor construction 30 years ago. He says electricity bills are rising in non-building states (NY, CA) and falling in Texas.

insights.headline: AI is 75% of Q1 GDP growth
insights.body: Sachs cites that AI accounts for 75% of GDP growth in Q1, with the boom extending beyond Silicon Valley into a construction and blue-collar boom featuring 25-30% wage increases for construction workers. He notes AI ranked only 29th of 39 issues in voter salience despite its unpopularity.

insights.headline: No evidence AI has lifted S&P margins yet
insights.body: Chamath insists there is 'not a scintilla of evidence' AI has lifted S&P 500 operating margins, predicting a reckoning in ~500 days where buyers of tokens must show measurable benefit. Brad counters margins rose 200bps to 13% with flat 3% headcount growth, but concedes it could be post-COVID 'age of fitness' rather than AI.

insights.headline: Elon gets a premium because rivals stopped innovating
insights.body: Chamath says Apple, Google, Meta and Amazon are fairly valued—'Elon World gets a premium' because everyone else has stopped innovating and only knows how to 'draw more blood from the stone.' The market and retail are signaling that incremental ad-targeting does nothing for society.

insights.headline: Tesla and SpaceX will merge into 'Elon Corp'
insights.body: Chamath predicts Tesla and SpaceX merge into a single 'Elon Corp' by end of year or mid next year, creating one asset trading at an unexplainable premium. He frames the eventual SpaceX IPO trading at 40-50x revenue—~$2T on $40-50B next-year revenue.

action_items: When evaluating AI lab revenue, judge it against power and compute supply—not demand—because that is the true binding constraint.
Track the ~500-day 'reckoning' window Chamath flags: watch for enterprises tracing spend (X) directly to higher margins (Y) before assuming AI ROI is real.
If you invest around the AI boom, note the relative cheapness of memory stocks (SK Hynix ~5x, Samsung ~6x, Micron ~7x) versus hyperscalers, per Altimeter's positioning.
Demand KYC—not pre-release approval—as the practical safety guardrail for frontier model API access, especially during preview periods.
Discount headlines about an 'FDA for AI' and AI job destruction; verify against primary sources, since both were contested as fake or premature on this episode.
